Subject: SSQ: PII segmentation, privileged cache access and evidence request

Hi Rohan,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call last week. As part of HealthCorp's vendor DPA annex we need a short package of evidence on a few privacy/security questions before our legal team signs off:

- A dataflow diagram showing where PII enters your platform, how it is tokenized/segmented, and which components handle unredacted PII vs derived embeddings/KV cache.
- Inventory of subprocessors that may interact with KV cache or derived artifacts (e.g., partner monitoring, SRE tools).
- A short attestation or statement about who has privileged access to in-memory KV caches and under what conditions (human access, break-glass procedures).
- A copy of latest KMS attestation or proof of key custody for customer-specific keys.

Can you send these artifacts (diagram + attestation + access matrix) by end of day June 3? If any of these require a different cadence please flag now — we can route to our security review team for a deeper chat.

Best,
Elena

Rohan / team — draft artifacts attached. Quick notes to include in the reply to HealthCorp:

- KMS: attached kms-attestation-2027-05.pdf. Keys are customer-scoped when requested via Private deployment; for hosted use we use envelope encryption where customer data keys are encrypted with our control-plane keys. The attestation includes key custody controls and rotation cadence.

- KV cache human access: by default there is no human access to live KV caches. SRE engineering can access ephemeral in-memory state only during a security-reviewed incident using break-glass flow. That flow requires a 4-eyes approval (SRE + InfoSec) and is logged in the incident audit trail (Ticket ID + JIRA link).

- Access matrix: attached access-matrix-roles.xlsx — contains role names (SRE, PlatformOps, SecurityOps, SE), justification, least-privilege scope, and last access review date.

- Subprocessors: Jonas added the short list to the Drive link; the only third parties that may see derived telemetry are our monitoring provider and a managed backup partner, both of whom are contractually limited to transient telemetry and never persist raw PII.

Recommend we provide the diagram + KMS attestation + access matrix and propose a 30-minute follow-up if HealthCorp needs signed attestations.

— Mina

Elena — thanks for the clarifying questions. Summary responses below and attached artifacts; let me know if you want any edits for the annex language.

- Cross-border replication: For Redwood-hosted customers, derived artifacts (embeddings and transient KV cache entries) are logically tenant-scoped and by default may be routed to the nearest region for performance. For HealthCorp (EU data subject), we can enable region-locking so that derived artifacts and KV cache are constrained to eu-central-1. We have documented region-locking as a configuration option in the onboarding playbook.

- Retention: KV cache entries are ephemeral by default with a TTL tuned per workload (default 24 hours for typical generation sessions). Persistent telemetry (logs and aggregated metrics) is retained 90 days by default; we can offer a reduced telemetry retention for enterprise contracts. If you need the retention excerpt for the DPA annex, use the paragraph below (paste-ready):

"Redwood maintains transient inference caches for performance; these caches are ephemeral and are not used as a persistent datastore for customer PII. Default TTL for ephemeral caches is 24 hours; persistent telemetry is retained for 90 days unless otherwise contracted. All access is governed by least-privilege roles and break-glass procedures described in the attached access matrix."

- Human/privileged access & DocuSign: Confirmed. Human access to unredacted in-memory KV cache is not routine and occurs only during incident response with InfoSec-approved break-glass. We will produce a DocuSign attestation for signature — link to follow.

Attachments included in this message: redwood-pii-dataflow-v1.png, kms-attestation-2027-05.pdf, access-matrix-roles.xlsx.

Next steps: we will send the DocuSign attestation by EOD tomorrow and schedule a 30-minute call if you'd like a walkthrough of the dataflow and break-glass logs.
